subject: Next steps: procurement & marketplace path for Redwood
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Lopez <slopez@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: procurement & marketplace path for Redwood

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Call recap (30m):
- Primary use: inference for production search & summarization workloads (pilot: hosted API).
- Expected pilot budget: ~$3–5k (2–4 week trial), then move to committed capacity if performance/latency checks good.
- Procurement posture: finance prefers PO for production buys; procurement noted they like AWS Marketplace for consolidated billing but need to confirm details.

Commercial / procurement options (high-level):
- P-card (corporate card): easy for small pilot < $5k — fastest.
- Direct PO / invoice: Redwood can accept a PO and invoice with net terms (typical 30/45 days). We can send MSA + SOW and process the PO.
- Cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure): marketplace purchase gives consolidated billing and can simplify procurement for some companies, but it requires onboarding/listing or a private offer. Timeline for listing/private-offer can be multi-week and may require additional paperwork.

Attachments I’m sharing: Redwood_MSA_v1.3.pdf (MSA draft), pricing-grid-Redwood.xlsx (pilot & reserved capacity options), SOC2-report-2025.pdf (security).

A few concrete asks so we can align the commercial path:
1) For the pilot, would procurement/finance be okay with a P-card charge under ~$5k?
2) Who on procurement should I loop in to get PO terms / vendor setup (name + email)?
3) Is LumenAI interested in purchasing via AWS (or GCP/Azure) Marketplace eventually? If so, we’ll coordinate marketplace ops and estimate a 4–8 week cadence for listing/private-offer depending on scope.

If helpful, I can 1) send a DocuSign for the MSA + SOW for a pilot, 2) open a private offer process with AWS if you want to pursue marketplace.

Would Friday morning PST work for a 30-min sync with procurement/finance to close the pilot path?

Thanks — Camila

-- 
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement & marketplace path for Redwood

Hi Camila — thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. A few quick answers: 

- Pilot: Procurement is fine with a P-card for an initial pilot <$5k. That will let us move quickly.
- Longer term: Finance prefers a PO for production/committed capacity. We’d likely want net-30 terms.
- Marketplace: We are very interested in AWS Marketplace for the consolidated billing and ease for our security review, but we need to understand whether Redwood requires a listing vs. can accept a private offer. Our procurement lead (Miguel) can evaluate which route is faster for us.

Procurement contact: Miguel Torres (miguel.torres@lumenai.com) — I’ve cc’d him. Procurement general inbox: procurement@lumenai.com.

Can you confirm: 1) if you accept P-card for pilot, 2) what the process is to set up a private offer on AWS Marketplace (what docs you need from us), and 3) whether your MSA has any clauses we should flag for our legal team (I’ll have our counsel look once you send).

Best,
Sofia

--
Sofia Lopez
Head of Operations | LumenAI
slopez@lumenai.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@lumenai.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Lopez <slopez@lumenai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement & marketplace path for Redwood

Hi Miguel (and team) — great to meet you over email. Quick answers and detail on options so you can share with legal/procurement: 

1) P-card for pilot: yes, we can accept a corporate card for a one-off pilot under your $5k guidance. We’ll provision the pilot environment and issue the invoice/receipt upon payment.

2) Direct PO / Invoice: We accept POs against an inbound invoice. Typical steps: vendor setup (W-9/COI as needed), sign MSA + SOW, Redwood issues invoices per SOW milestones/monthly usage, and payment per net terms (Net 30/45 configurable). I’ve attached the MSA for review.

3) AWS Marketplace (private offer vs listing):
- Private Offer: fastest path if you want the benefits of marketplace billing without a public listing — requires agreement on price/terms and AWS Marketplace private-offer creation. We’ll need your AWS account ID and a contact for the private-offer flow. Estimated timeline: ~1–3 weeks once terms are agreed (depends on your finance/legal turnaround and AWS ops).
- Public Listing: longer (multi-week to couple months) and requires Redwood to publish an offer; good for longer-term marketplace strategy.

Attachments & links: MSA (Redwood_MSA_v1.3.pdf), pricing grid (pricing-grid-Redwood.xlsx), SOC2 (SOC2-report-2025.pdf), DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/Redwood-MSA-v1.3, AWS private-offer info: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/.

Next steps I suggest: 
A) For fastest time-to-pilot: Sofia/Miguel confirm P-card details and we’ll spin up pilot access this week.
B) Parallel: Legal can review the MSA (DocuSign link above). If you want net-30 on PO, mention that in the PO.
C) If Marketplace: send AWS account ID and we’ll kick off a private-offer request.

If useful, I can schedule a 30-min procurement/finance sync on Friday to close the pilot. What time works for you?

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Next steps: procurement & marketplace path for Redwood

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear options. A few items from procurement/finance side: 

- We can do the P-card for the pilot. Please let us know the billing descriptor so our card team can approve the charge.
- For production, we generally move to PO with net-30. We’ll need vendor setup docs (W-9 and COI) and the MSA for legal review.
- AWS Marketplace: we prefer a private offer if possible. Our AWS account ID is 1234-5678-9012. If you need additional company information (tax id, legal entity name, DUNS), let me know.

Can Redwood accept a P-card now and then convert to a PO for committed capacity? Also, does Redwood offer reserved/dedicated pricing that we should review vs hosted consumption pricing?

Regards,
Miguel

Thanks Miguel — great, appreciate the info. Quick confirmations and proposed next steps: 

1) P-card: yes — billing descriptor will be "REDWOOD*INFERENCE". I’ll share the invoice/receipt immediately after charge.

2) Vendor setup: I’m attaching the W-9 and COI in this thread (Redwood_MSA_v1.3.pdf includes legal entity info; separate W-9/COI are attached here). For the MSA, we use standard commercial terms; I’ve added redline notes for any common asks and will route legal questions to our contracts team if needed. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/Redwood-MSA-v1.3.

3) Marketplace private offer: we can start the private-offer flow against AWS account ID 1234-5678-9012. Our Marketplace ops person will need a contact and the PO/price expectation — I’ll introduce them after you confirm you want to proceed. Estimated internal timeline: ~1–3 weeks to finalize private offer once both sides sign off.

4) Pricing model: For pilots we recommend hosted consumption. If you plan to commit to steady throughput or dedicated GPU pools, reserved capacity (Dedicated) gives better unit economics — I attached the pricing grid (pricing-grid-Redwood.xlsx) that compares hosted vs reserved. If helpful I can model a 6-month commit for projected usage.

Next steps (proposed):
- Miguel/Sofia: confirm P-card payment window and send the card billing contact.
- Legal: review MSA via DocuSign and flag any high-priority redlines.
- If Marketplace: confirm private-offer route and we’ll exchange the minimal company info (DUNS/tax id) and pricing target.
- Can we meet Friday 11am PST for a 30-min procurement alignment? I’ve penciled that in but happy to move.

If you confirm the P-card, we’ll provision access and share API keys/console for the pilot within 24 hours of payment.

Best — Camila
